title: The necessity foreknowledge brings is hypothetical, of the consequence, of infallibility, not antecedent
source_text: XXVI. Uno verbo, sicut ex visione rerum praesentium inducitur quaedam earum necessitas, sed hypothetica tantum, & quae in Scholis dicitur necessitas consequens, sive consequentiae, quaeque optime consistit cum earum libertate, sive contingentia: sic etiam ex rerum futurarum praevisione, sequitur quidem eas necessario eventuras esse, sed necessitate tantum ex hypothesi, & quae dici solet infallibilitatis, quae non obstat quominus in se & absolute liberae sint, & contingentes. Nam si qua necessitas contingentiam & libertatem tollit, illa demum est quae dicitur antecedens atque absoluta, nec solum consequentiae, sed etiam consequentis.
pass_a_gloss: XXVI. In a word, just as from the sight of present things a certain necessity of them is induced, but hypothetical only, and which in the Schools is called consequent necessity, or necessity of the consequence, and which consists excellently with their liberty, or contingency: so also from the foresight of future things, it follows indeed that they will necessarily come to pass, but with necessity only from hypothesis, and which is wont to be called of infallibility, which does not hinder that they be in themselves and absolutely free, and contingent. For if any necessity takes away contingency and liberty, that at last is that which is called antecedent and absolute, and not only of the consequence, but also of the consequent.
pass_b_english: In short, seeing present things brings a certain necessity upon them, but only a hypothetical one. The schools call it consequent necessity, or the necessity of the consequence, and it fits perfectly well with their freedom or contingency.

So too the foresight of future things means that they will necessarily happen, but only by a necessity that rests on a hypothesis, usually called the necessity of infallibility. It does not stop them being free and contingent in themselves and absolutely.
The only necessity that removes contingency and freedom is the one called antecedent and absolute, which is a necessity not merely of the consequence but of the consequent as well.

choices.why: The Schools distinguish the necessity of the consequence (hypothetical) from the necessity of the consequent (absolute); the technical pair is kept so the argument stays exact.
